data.title: Product Backlog
data.tagline: A dynamic, ordered list of features, fixes, and improvements that a product may need next
data.learningOutcome: You can maintain an ordered, evolving, progressively refined product backlog and distinguish it from a roadmap or current delivery plan.
data.description: When a trip app receives both a payment incident and a map-export idea, the team can reorder items using product goals, risk, and new evidence. Items near the top are usually clearer, but backlog inclusion does not promise a date or delivery.

learning.assumes: You have features, defects, improvements, and technical work competing for attention.
learning.outcome: You can maintain an ordered, evolving, progressively refined product backlog and distinguish it from a roadmap or current delivery plan.

explanation.title: Collect different kinds of candidate work
explanation.text: Features, defects, experience improvements, and necessary technical work can all enter the list.

explanation.title: Use order to express the current judgment
explanation.text: Order reflects value, risk, dependencies, and evidence rather than a permanent priority label.

explanation.title: Add detail as work gets closer
explanation.text: Near-term items need clear scope and completion conditions; distant ideas can wait for more evidence.

data.boundary: A Product Backlog orders candidate work, a Product Roadmap communicates goals and direction, and a Gantt Chart schedules selected tasks. A backlog item is not automatically a delivery commitment.

lessonPractice.title: A payment failure affects every order, while the team also receives a map-color suggestion. How should the product backlog change?

options.label: Verify the impact, move the payment failure upward with clearer acceptance conditions, and keep the color idea lower while gathering evidence
options.feedback: Correct. The order can change with risk and evidence. Near-term items need more clarity than distant ideas.

options.label: Append every new item by arrival time and never change the existing order
options.feedback: A product backlog is dynamic. Keeping the old order after new risk appears removes its decision value.

options.label: Assign a release date to every item and promise that all of them will ship
options.feedback: Being in the backlog means an item is considered, not that its scope or release date is committed.

data.agentPrompt: Organize these features, defects, and improvements into a product backlog. Propose an order using the product goal, user impact, risk, and evidence I provide, and explain each choice. Mark unsupported judgments as assumptions. Add the problem, scope, and acceptance conditions to near-term items while keeping distant items brief. Recommend the order without promising dates or deleting lower items.
